raw_question_text: A 800N Cylinder is supported by the frame ABC, figure 1 which is hinged at A, and rests against wall AD. Determine the reactions at A, B, C and D.
The body shown in figure 2 is acted upon by four forces. Determine the resultant.

What do you understand by resultant of a force system and which are the methods used for determining the resulting of coplanar concurrent force system? Four forces having magnitudes of 20N, 40N, 60N and 80N respectively, are acting along the four sides (1m each), of a square ABCD taken in order, as shown in figure 3. Determine the magnitude and direction of the resultant force.
Determine the y coordinate of the centroid of a uniform triangular lamina as shown in Figure 4.
Find the magnitude and direction of the resultant force. Also find the position of the resultant force from point P of the bar PS.
Determine x,y,z, components of 750 N and 900 N and also the angles θ x, θy and θz that the force forms with coordinate axes shown in figure 2.

What is the least value of P to cause motion of the system shown in figure 3 towards the right. Also find θ. Assume coefficient of friction to be 0.2. Body A and B weighs 900 N and 650 N respectively.

A 120 wedge resting on a horizontal floor supports a block of weight 1200 N as shown in Figure 4. The block is to be raised by applying a horizontal force P to the wedge. Assume coefficient of friction between all contact surfaces to be 0.28. Determine minimum horizontal force applied to the wedge to raise the block.
Locate the centroid of the shaded area as shown in Figure 5.
Find the moment of inertia about Y axis of the shaded area under the second degree curve as shown in Figure 6.
Determine the radius of gyration in m about the centroidal X axis of the casting as shown in figure 7.
Block A has a weight of 300 N and block B has a weight of 50 N. Determine the speed of block A after it moves 2 m down the plane, starting from the rest.

The double pulley shown in figure 9 has a mass of 3 kg and a radius of gyration of 100 mm. knowing that pulley is at rest, a force of 24 N is applied to cord B, determine the velocity of the centre of the pulley after 1.5 sec and tension in cord C.
Two systems of forces are shown in figure 1. Are they equivalent?

The beam EF in figure 2 weighs 120 N/m and carries the 600 -N weight at its end. It is supported by a ball -and-socket joint at E and the cables AB and CD. Determine the tensions in AB and CD. Find the joint reactions at E. All dimensions are in cm.

A 150 wedge has to be driven downwards for moving the block B of 750 N weight as shown in figure 3. If the angle of friction for all surfaces is 10 o, find the force P required to move the wedge. What will be the value of P if friction on horizontal floor and vertical wall neglected? The coefficient of friction between the wedge and block remain same.
Calculate the moment of inertia of the composite area shown in figure 4 about the two centroidal axes and its polar moment of inertia.
Compute the moment of inertia of the cast-iron flywheel shown in figure 5. The density of cast iron is 7200 kg/m3. All dimensions are mm.
The cable exerts a tension of 2 kN on the fixed bracket at A as shown in the figure 1. Write the vector expression for the tension T.

Three cylinders are placed in a rectangular ditch as shown in figure 2. Neglecting friction, determine the reaction between cylinder A and the vertical wall. Weights of cylinders A, B, C are 75 N, 200 N 100N and Radius is 100 mm, 150 mm, 125 mm respectively.

A 75 N vertical force is applied to the end of a bar 3 m long which is attached to a shaft at O as shown in figure 3. Determine: i) The moment of the 75 N force about O ii) The magnitude of the horizontal force applied at A which creates the same moment about O iii) The smallest force applied at A which creates the same moment about O iv) How far from the shaft at O a 200 N vertical force must act to create the same moment about O?

Two identical planes AC and BC, inclined at 60 0 and 300 to the horizontal meet at C as shown in figure 4. A load of 1000 N rests on the inclined plane BC and is tied by a rope passing over a pulley to a block weighing W Newton and resting on the plane AC. If the coefficient of friction between the load and the plane BC is 0.28 and that between the block and the plane AC is 0.20, find the least and greatest values of W for the equilibrium of the system.

Determine the magnitude and direction of the friction force acting on the 100-kg block shown in the figure 5 if, first, P = 500 N and, second, P = 100 N are applied. The coefficient of static friction is 0.20, and the coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.17. The forces are applied with the block initially at rest.
A corner of radius 20 mm is cut off from a square plate of 40 mm side as shown in the figure 6. Find the moment of inertia of the remaining plate about its axes of symmetry.
With respect to the coordinate axes x and y, locate the centroid of the shaded area shown in the figure 7.

A uniform wire is bent into the shape as shown in the figure 8. The straight segments lie in the X-Z plane and the line of 80 mm length makes an angle of 300 with the X-axis. The semi-circular segment is in the X-Y plane. Locate the centroid of the wire.

Two bodies A and B of mass 80 kg and 20 kg are connected by a thread and move along a rough horizontal plane under the action of a force 400 N applied to the first body of mass 80 kg as shown in Figure 9. The coefficient of friction between the sliding surfaces of the bodies and the plane is 0.3. Determine the acceleration of the two bodies and the tension in the thread, using D'Alembert's principle.
Calculate the magnitude of the moment about the point 'O' of the 600-N force as shown in figure 1.
A man raises a 10 kg joist of 4 m length by pulling on a rope attached to the joist as shown in the figure 2. At this instant, find tension in the rope and reaction at end A of joist.
Determine and locate the resultant R of the two forces and one couple acting on the I-beam as shown in figure 3.

Three bars pinned together at B and C and supported by hinges at A and D as shown in the figure 4 form a four link mechanism. Determine the value of P which is required to hold the system in equilibrium.

Two block of weight W 1 = 50 N and W 2 = 50 N are resting on a rough inclined plane as shown in the figure 5. If μ = 0.3 for W 1 and plane and μ = 0.2 for W 2 and plane, find the inclination of the plane for which slipping will impend.

A block overlaying a 100 wedge on a horizontal floor, leaning against a vertical wall, and weighing 2000 N is to be raised by applying a horizontal force to the wedge as shown in figure 6. Assuming coefficient of friction for all contact surfaces is 0.25, determine the minimum horizontal force to be applied to raise the block.
Determine the co-ordinates of centroid of the shaded area enclosed by a parabola 4y = x 2 and a straight line x - y = 0 as shown in figure 7.
Find the moment of inertia of the shaded area shown in the figure 8 about the edge AB.

The 3000 N block starting from rest as shown in the figure 9 slides down a 50 0 inclined plane. After moving 2 m it strikes spring whose modulus is 20 N/mm. If the coefficient of friction between the block and inclined plane is 0.2, determine the maximum deformation of the spring and the maximum velocity of the block.
After the block in the figure 10 has moved 3 m from rest, the constant force P is removed. Find the velocity of the block when it returns to its initial position.
